title: Emergent trans-moiré orbitals and topology in rhombohedral graphene
authors: Yuqin Wang, Jian Xie, Yi-Jie Wang, Jiajun Zhang, Yiting Gao, Zaizhe Zhang, Da Yi, Yan Xie, Jingjing Shi, Guanqin Zhao, Chengyu Xiong, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zhi-Da Song, Xiaobo Lu, Yi Chen
abstract: The fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect (FQAHE) exhibited in fractional Chern insulators has recently been demonstrated in twisted MoTe2 and rhombohedral graphene/hBN moiré superlattices, promising new routes toward topological quantum computation. Central to realizing this promise is the understanding of the underlying microscopic mechanism. This, however, remains elusive in the case of rhombohedral graphene, with the crux being its two seemingly paradoxical conditions: a pronounced small-twist-angle (θ) moiré interface, yet only when electrons are kept distant from it. Here, by scanning tunnelling microscopic imaging with both conditions fulfilled, we capture dramatic electronic structure reshaping in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene by unforeseen 'trans-moiré orbitals', which emerge on the other, distant side of the moiré interface but nevertheless enforce the moiré periodicity at all measured fillings. We visualize a hierarchy of spatially and energetically distinct trans-moiré orbitals which doped electrons must sequentially occupy--the lowest-energy orbital, expectedly responsible for the FQAHE at small fillings, carries a hollow-cage-like shape. Remarkably, these trans-moiré orbitals vanish at θ {\gtrsim} 1°, and so do QAHE plateaus in similar devices. Simulations reveal an interaction-driven charge-redistribution mechanism which shapes the trans-moiré orbitals and corresponding Chern minibands. With our findings providing the missing microscopic link, the paradoxical conditions find a natural explanation: electrons are not simply kept distant from a small-θ moiré interface; they are forced into topological trans-moiré orbitals, forged precisely under such conditions. Our microscopic diagnostics unlocks a wide range of possible 'synthetic' FQAHE platforms.
summary: The paper reports the discovery of 'trans-moiré orbitals' in rhombohedral graphene/hBN moiré superlattices. These orbitals emerge on the side distant from the primary moiré interface and are responsible for stabilizing topological features like the FQAHE. The findings resolve a long-standing paradox by showing that electron interactions force the system into these specific, topologically active orbital states.
main_problem: The study aims to resolve the microscopic mechanism behind the Fractional Quantum Anomalous Hall Effect (FQAHE) in rhombohedral graphene moiré superlattices, specifically addressing the paradox of observing a small-twist-angle interface only when electrons are kept distant from it.
main_result: The authors discovered emergent 'trans-moiré orbitals' on the moiré-distant surface, which enforce moiré periodicity and vanish at critical twist angles ($	heta \sim 1^\circ$), providing a microscopic explanation for the topological effects observed.
method: The research combines Scanning Tunneling Microscopy/Spectroscopy (STM/STS) measurements with self-consistent mean-field calculations to map out the electronic structure reshaping.
model_or_system: The physical system is rhombohedral hexalayer graphene ($	ext{R6G}$) stacked on hexagonal boron nitride ($	ext{hBN}$), forming a moiré superlattice. The electronic properties are tuned by gate voltage and controlled by the moiré twist angle ($	heta$).
key_observables: Trans-moiré orbitals (e.g., hollow-cage shape), flat-band renormalization strength, Chern minibands, and quantized Hall plateaus.
important_parameters: Moiré twist angle ($	heta$), filling factor ($v$), and gate voltage ($V_{	ext{bg}}$).
main_assumptions: The mechanism is attributed to an interaction-driven charge-redistribution across layers, forcing electrons into these topological orbitals.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate STM topographies and dI/dV spectra showing moiré renormalization on the distant surface for small $	heta$, contrasting with null results at large $	heta$. Simulations map these emergent orbitals to theoretical Chern minibands.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem (FQAHE mechanism), presents experimental evidence via STM mapping of trans-moiré orbitals under specific twist angles, explains this emergence through interaction-driven charge redistribution, and concludes by linking this finding to a general platform for synthetic FQAHE realization.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses emergent topological phases in moiré systems using spectroscopic measurements, which is highly relevant for understanding correlated electron behavior in engineered quantum materials.
